verses.text: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that the people of Israel were coming along the road to Atharim. He attacked Israel and captured some of them.
Then Israel made a special promise to the LORD: "If you will hand these people over to us, we will completely destroy their towns."
The LORD listened to Israel and handed the Canaanites over to them. They completely destroyed them and their towns, so the place was called Hormah, which means destruction.
The people of Israel set out from Mount Hor along the road to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient on the way.
They spoke against God and against Moses: "Why did you bring us out of Egypt to die in the desert? There is no bread and no water, and we hate this awful food!"
So the LORD sent poisonous snakes among the people. They bit the people, and many of the Israelites died.
The people came to Moses and said, "We sinned when we spoke against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD to take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Make a model of a poisonous snake and put it on a pole. Anyone who is bitten can look at it and live."
So Moses made a bronze snake and put it on a pole. Whenever someone was bitten by a snake and looked at the bronze snake, he lived.
The people of Israel moved on and camped at Oboth.
Then they left Oboth and camped at Iye Abarim, in the desert facing Moab toward the sunrise.
From there they moved on and camped in the Zered Valley.
From there they moved on and camped on the other side of the Arnon River, in the desert that reaches into Amorite land. The Arnon is the border between Moab and the Amorites.
That is why the Book of the Wars of the LORD speaks of "Waheb in Suphah, and the valleys of the Arnon,
and the slopes of the valleys that reach to the town of Ar and lie along the border of Moab."
From there they went on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people together, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song: "Spring up, O well! Sing about it!
Sing about the well that the leaders dug, that the important men of the people dug with their royal sticks and walking sticks." From the desert they went on to Mattanah,
from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
From Bamoth they went to the valley in Moab, where the top of Mount Pisgah looks out over the wasteland.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites, to say:
"Let us pass through your country. We will not go into any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King's Highway until we have passed through your land."
But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his land. He gathered his whole army and marched out into the desert to fight Israel. When he reached Jahaz, he attacked Israel.
But Israel defeated him in battle and took over his land from the Arnon River to the Jabbok River, as far as the land of the Ammonites, because the Ammonite border was strongly protected.
Israel took all the Amorite towns and settled in them, including Heshbon and all its villages.
Heshbon was the city of Sihon, king of the Amorites. He had fought against the earlier king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon River.
That is why the poets say: "Come to Heshbon! Let the city of Sihon be rebuilt and made strong again.
For fire came out from Heshbon, a flame from Sihon's city. It burned up Ar in Moab, and the rulers of the hills by the Arnon.
How terrible for you, Moab! You are destroyed, you people who worship the god Chemosh! He has let his sons run away and his daughters be captured by Sihon, king of the Amorites.
But we have shot them down. Heshbon is destroyed all the way to Dibon. We have destroyed them as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba."
So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to explore the town of Jazer. The Israelites captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who lived there.
Then they turned and went up along the road to Bashan. Og, king of Bashan, marched out with his whole army to fight them at Edrei.

But the LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, with all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon."
So they defeated Og, his sons, and his whole army, leaving no survivors, and they took over his land.
